title: Sales Billing Control Map
purpose: Separate billing eligibility, plan timing, billing type, copy control, split/convergence, document creation and downstream financial effects into traceable controls.
mental_model: Start before VF04. First prove why the reference is billable.
Do not mix billing relevance with billing quantity, billing type, pricing type, or invoice split.
A correct billing document can still carry an incorrect inherited value if copying control intentionally preserved it.
Unexpected invoice count is a grouping problem until split analysis proves otherwise.

stages.title: Define billing basis and eligibility
stages.question: Is the sales or delivery reference billable, on which basis, and is it due now?

stages.title: Build billing-plan timing when required
stages.question: Which periodic or milestone date controls the next billing event?
stages.result: plan type + due date + amount/percentage + date status

stages.title: Choose the target billing type
stages.question: What billing document type should this reference create?

stages.title: Transfer data, quantity and pricing
stages.question: What is copied from the reference, what is recalculated, and which quantity is billed?
stages.result: target billing data + pricing/quantity transfer behavior

stages.title: Group or split billable items
stages.question: Can the items share one billing header or do differences force several documents?

stages.title: Create and hand off the billing document
stages.question: Did the billable result become the expected billing document, FI event and output object?

copy_boundaries.rule: Billing relevance defines the business basis; copying control can still decide which source quantity is transferred for billing.
The pricing type in billing copying control decides whether pricing conditions are copied, redetermined, or combined according to the configured pricing behavior.

copy_boundaries.topic: Payment terms and other header data
copy_boundaries.rule: Billing data normally follows the reference and copying/data-transfer logic. A copying requirement or data-transfer routine can intentionally source selected data, such as payment terms, from another owner such as customer master data.
How reference and assignment numbers are transferred can itself create different billing headers and therefore an invoice split.

failure_drills.symptom: Sales order or delivery is complete but is missing from the billing due list.
failure_drills.wrong_first_move: Change the billing type or run VF01 manually.
failure_drills.lead_conclusion: Eligibility is upstream of document creation. Prove why the reference is not due before bypassing the due list.

failure_drills.symptom: A milestone invoice is not available although the project team expects it.
failure_drills.lead_conclusion: Milestone timing belongs to the billing plan. The due list only consumes the resulting plan status.

failure_drills.symptom: The reference proposes the wrong invoice or credit/debit memo type.
failure_drills.lead_conclusion: Billing type is decided before posting. Account determination is downstream and cannot repair a wrong billing transaction type.

failure_drills.symptom: Invoice price differs from the sales order although the expected condition record exists.
failure_drills.lead_conclusion: Billing may intentionally reprice. Prove the copy-control pricing boundary before touching pricing master data.

failure_drills.symptom: Two deliveries for the same customer create separate invoices.
failure_drills.lead_conclusion: A standard split criterion is evidence, not a defect. Custom logic comes only after the differing owner is understood.

failure_drills.symptom: One sales order creates several invoices.
failure_drills.wrong_first_move: Assume collective billing configuration is broken.
proof_path: item-level values copied to billing header
failure_drills.lead_conclusion: A single reference document does not guarantee a single billing document. Item differences can force multiple target headers.
